title: 石灰吟
author: 于谦
intro: A poem about limestone — hammered out of the mountain, burned in fire, crushed to powder — that is really about a person who will keep his integrity whatever it costs. Chinese schoolchildren learn it as a model of courage.
analysis: 这首诗表面写石灰怎么做成：先从深山里一锤一凿地开采石头，再放进烈火里烧，最后变成白色的粉末。可是每一句都在写人。“若等闲”是说把烈火焚烧看得很平常；“粉骨碎身浑不怕”是说就算粉身碎骨也完全不怕；最后一句点明心愿：要把清清白白留在人间。“清白”一语双关（一个词有两层意思）：石灰是白色的，人也要品格干净、不做坏事。这种借写一样东西来表达自己志向的写法叫“托物言志”。传说于谦十几岁时写了这首诗，后来他真的做到了：保卫北京立了大功，最后却被冤杀，一生清廉。诗和人一致，所以特别打动人。
analysisEn:
On the surface this is about how lime is made. Limestone is cut out of the deep mountains with a thousand hammer blows, then burned in a fierce kiln, and finally crumbles into white powder that is used to whitewash walls. But every line is also about a person.

“As if it were nothing” (若等闲) means facing the fire calmly. “Bones ground to powder, body broken — not afraid at all” is a vow to accept any suffering. The last line states the wish: to leave something clean and white in the world. The word 清白 works on two levels — lime is white, and a person who is 清白 is honest, clean, untouched by corruption. Writing about an object in order to state your own ideals is called 托物言志 (“using a thing to express one’s aims”), a very common method in Chinese poetry.

Tradition says Yu Qian wrote this as a teenager, and his life matched the poem: he saved Beijing in a national crisis, stayed famously honest, and was later executed on false charges. Because the poet lived what he wrote, the poem is still quoted when people talk about integrity, and it is in every primary-school textbook.
background: Yu Qian (1398–1457) was a Ming official who organised the defence of Beijing in 1449, after the emperor was captured by Mongol forces. He was executed in 1457 after a palace coup and later cleared of all charges. The poem is traditionally said to be a work of his youth, though the attribution has been questioned.
pronunciation: 凿 záo；焚 fén；浑 hún（全、完全）；间 jiān。
version: 采用统编教材（六年级下册）文本：“粉骨碎身浑不怕”。通行本亦多作“粉身碎骨浑不怕”；另有“千锤万击出深山”的异文，网站不用。

lines.py: qiān chuí wàn záo chū shēn shān
lines.lit: A thousand hammer blows, ten thousand chisel strokes — out of the deep mountain;
lines.en: Hammered and chiselled out of the deep mountain,

lines.py: liè huǒ fén shāo ruò děng xián
lines.lit: burned by fierce fire, as if it were ordinary.
lines.en: it takes the blazing fire as if it were nothing.

lines.py: fěn gǔ suì shēn hún bù pà
lines.lit: Bones powdered, body broken — not afraid at all,
lines.en: Ground to powder, body and bone, it has no fear —

lines.py: yào liú qīng bái zài rén jiān
lines.lit: it wants to leave purity and whiteness in the human world.
lines.en: it only wants to leave something clean and white in this world.

words.note: 现代汉语书面语仍用，如“焚烧垃圾”。
古语词，现代汉语说“好像”；成语“若无其事”还在用。
古义；现代汉语有“等闲视之”（不当回事）。

words.en: bones ground to powder, body broken — to die for a cause
words.note: 现代汉语常说“粉身碎骨”。
古义，现代汉语说“完全”“全”；今天“浑”多指“浑浊”。

words.en: pure and white; (of a person) honest, blameless
words.note: 现代汉语仍用，如“他是清白的”“清清白白做人”。
现代汉语仍用，如“人间天堂”。

imagery.name: 石灰
imagery.zh: 石灰经过开采、焚烧、粉碎仍然洁白，象征诗人不怕牺牲、坚守清白的品格。
imagery.en: Lime stays white after being quarried, burned and crushed — the poet’s integrity under any ordeal.

imagery.name: 火
imagery.zh: 烈火代表严酷的考验和迫害，石灰把它看得很平常，显出不怕困难的勇气。
imagery.en: The fierce fire stands for harsh trials and persecution; the lime treats it as nothing, showing courage.
